brief: SOX was priced for an AI slowdown. The market read slower frontier AI development as a capex cut and took SOX from roughly 23x to 13.85x on Bloomberg's blended 24-month forward earnings. But hyperscaler capex plans remain intact through 2027/28 per Goldman's Privorotsky, Korea's semiconductor exports surged 259.4% YoY in the first 20 days of September (total exports +78.3%), and earnings estimates have held up. That gap between what was priced and what is happening is closing, driving the squeeze. SOX broke its short-term downtrend and is pushing above its 100-day moving average, with 12,800 as the next level, a close above which could revive an all-time-high narrative. SOX's P/E multiple is near multi-year lows even as compute stays scarce and workloads grow. Permitting, not capex appetite, is flagged as the bigger constraint on data-center buildout, with impact differing across electrical, power, cooling, and interconnect names. The note reiterates a prior call flagging cheap 1-month 110%-strike SOX calls 10 sessions ago, now repriced fast, and advises rolling some exposure to higher strikes and banking part of the gain.
